 Search The Site Gear Up For Game Day: UTEP Miners Gear Up For Game Day: UTEP Miners
 Cody Tucker Cody Tucker Published: November 13, 2026 HATTIESBURG, MS - SEPTEMBER 28: UTEP Miners head coach Dana Dimel looks on during the Southern Miss Golden Eagles game versus the UTEP Miners on September 28, 2019, at Carlisle-Faulkner Field at M.M. Roberts Stadium in Hattiesburg, MS. (Photo by Bobby McDuffie/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Share on Facebook 
 Share on Twitter 
 EL PASO, Texas -- It's always good to be back in the Lone Star State.
 Whataburger. Award-winning barbecue. Cold beer.
 7220 Sports The only thing that would make this trip any better, on a personal level, is if Dana Dimel was still here. Both in El Paso and in person.
 Wyoming's former head coach from 1997-99 took the reins of the UTEP program back in 2018. He spent six seasons in this dusty border town, winning just 20 games. Always warm and inviting, the life-long football man died in December of 2024. He was just 62.
 In the spring of 2019, I made the trek down here to meet with the man who broke my heart so many years ago. I'll never forget when he left for the same job at the University of Houston. I'm not sure I was over Joe Tiller leaving yet, to be honest.
 Wyoming fans, in those days, were always worried about losing coaches to bigger programs.
 But Houston? Come on.
 Dimel admitted to me that afternoon in his office high above the famed Sun Bowl that he almost immediately knew he had made a mistake leaving Laramie. That was the place he cut his teeth. He also married his beloved wife Julie at the 50-yard line inside War Memorial Stadium.
 He was always upset the school opted for turf instead of keeping the natural grass.
 Yes, he received a massive pay raise to lead the Cougars. He was also a veteran in recruiting the state of Texas. A dose of reality hit, he said, when he entered the Houston Astrodome for the annual spring game only to see a handful of fans in the stands.
 "The three most important people in Wyoming are the governor, the football coach and the basketball coach," he was once told by a Cowboys' fan. "And it wasn't always necessarily in that order.
 "The people there are so passionate."
 He missed that.
 He would go on to win only eight games in three seasons at UH. Art Briles, with Dimel's recruits, won seven the following year.
 The Ohio native would go on to coach at Arizona and again at Kansas State before landing the gig in El Paso.
 During his brief Wyoming tenure, Dimel, 34, finished 22-13 overall. His teams were known for going toe-to-toe with the big dogs of college football -- Ohio State, Colorado and Georgia -- and coming up just short. Same can be said for the conference races and bowl appearances.
 Still, Iowa called. So did Oklahoma and South Carolina. Those opportunities fell through. Houston ultimately won out.
 "There were a couple of variables," he added. "One, Houston was going to pay me $750,000 a year. I was making $195,000 at Laramie. So, that was a no-brainer. Secondly, I was going to have to make some moves with friends (in the coaching staff). They weren't grooving really well in the mix of what we were doing."
 In hindsight, he admitted a lack of patience, regretably, got the best of him.
 "I could've left it better," he said of his departure from Laramie. "They gave me my first job, and I have nothing but unbelievable memories there. The one thing that helped me there is, anyone who really knew me knows how I respect and treat people. They know who I am as a person. You can be mad at me, but you know what kind of quality individual I am.”
 I saw it firsthand. Dimel was one of a kind and dearly missed. I will certainly be thinking about him Saturday night.
 He'll have the best seat in the house as his former teams go head-to-head.
 Here is all you need to know -- and the links -- for Saturday night's tilt in Texas:
